concept: Role play develops empathy and social/interpersonal skills (affective domain)
must_teach: Role play: learners act as another person to experience their situation and feelings; it builds empathy, attitudes and interpersonal skills, not recall, calculation or drawing.

concept: Morrison's assimilation step: supervised individual study until mastery
must_teach: Morrison's understanding-level steps are exploration, presentation, assimilation, organisation, recitation; assimilation is the longest step of supervised individual study with testing and re-teaching.

concept: Anecdotal record is a qualitative evaluation tool
must_teach: An anecdotal record is a brief written description of a significant incident in a student's behaviour (qualitative); test scores, percentile ranks and standard scores are quantitative.

concept: McClelland proposed achievement motivation theory (need for achievement)
must_teach: McClelland: need for achievement (n-Ach), preference for moderately difficult tasks and feedback; Maslow: hierarchy of needs; Rogers: humanistic/facilitation; Lewin: field theory, leadership styles.

concept: Vygotsky's approach is social (socio-cultural) constructivism
must_teach: Piaget = cognitive (individual) constructivism; Vygotsky = social/socio-cultural constructivism stressing interaction with others and culture.

concept: Base of Dale's Cone is direct purposeful experience
must_teach: Dale's Cone base = direct purposeful experiences (most concrete); moving up through contrived experiences, demonstrations, exhibits, motion pictures, visual symbols to verbal symbols at the apex (most abstract).

concept: ABCD model of objectives: Audience, Behaviour, Condition, Degree
must_teach: ABCD objectives: Audience (who), Behaviour (what), Condition (circumstances), Degree (how well); extends Mager's performance, condition, criterion.

concept: Formative evaluation = assessment for learning
must_teach: Formative = assessment for learning (used to improve learning during the process); summative = assessment of learning; self-assessment = assessment as learning; placement/diagnostic come before.

concept: Reflective level is associated with problem-solving
must_teach: Memory level: drill, recitation, rote; understanding level: explanation, generalisation; reflective level: problem-solving and independent inquiry.

concept: E-portfolio: digital collection of student work, reflections and feedback
must_teach: An e-portfolio stores a student's selected work electronically with reflections and teacher comments, showing growth over time.

concept: Full form of SWAYAM
must_teach: SWAYAM = Study Webs of Active-Learning for Young Aspiring Minds; principles access, equity, quality; four quadrants: video, reading material, self-assessment tests, discussion forum.

concept: Verb 'design' signals the Create level of revised Bloom
must_teach: Create verbs: design, construct, compose, formulate, plan; Remember: list, define; Understand: explain, summarise; Apply: solve, demonstrate.

concept: Sternberg's triarchic theory of intelligence
must_teach: Sternberg: triarchic (analytical, creative, practical); Spearman: two-factor; Thurstone: group-factor (primary mental abilities); Thomson: sampling theory.

concept: Highest level of Bloom's original (1956) cognitive taxonomy is Evaluation
must_teach: 1956 order: Knowledge, Comprehension, Application, Analysis, Synthesis, Evaluation; 2001 revision puts Create (renamed Synthesis) above Evaluate.

concept: Adults are motivated mainly by internal needs (Knowles)
must_teach: Knowles: adult motivation is chiefly internal (self-esteem, job satisfaction, quality of life, growth); external pressure, fear, small rewards typify children.

concept: Mastery learning relies on criterion-referenced tests
must_teach: Bloom's mastery learning sets a fixed standard per unit (e.g. 80%) that every learner must reach, checked by criterion-referenced (formative) tests followed by correctives.

concept: SGPA = sum(credits x grade points) / total credits of courses taken
must_teach: SGPA = sum of (course credits x grade points) / sum of course credits for the semester; not divided by number of courses.

concept: Inclusive classroom supports all learners including those with disabilities
must_teach: Inclusion: learners of all abilities and backgrounds, including those with disabilities, learn together with needed supports; required under RPwD Act 2016; not segregation or one method for all.

concept: Skill of reinforcement: praise such as 'Good, well explained!'
must_teach: Reinforcement skill: encouraging desired responses with praise, nods, smiles; probing = follow-up questions; illustrating = examples; closure = consolidating at end.

concept: Item analysis gives difficulty value and discriminating power
must_teach: Item analysis after tryout finds each item's difficulty (proportion correct), discrimination (high vs low scorers) and distractor functioning.

concept: 'Models of Teaching' written by Joyce and Weil
must_teach: Joyce & Weil: Models of Teaching, four families (information-processing, social, personal, behavioural); Flanders/Amidon: interaction analysis; Allen/Ryan: micro-teaching; Bloom/Krathwohl: taxonomy.

concept: Problem-solving method develops scientific thinking
must_teach: Problem-solving follows scientific method steps (define problem, gather data, hypothesise, test, conclude) and develops reasoning and scientific attitude.

concept: Last Herbartian step is application
must_teach: Herbartian five steps: preparation, presentation, comparison/association, generalisation, application (original had clarity, association, system, method); recitation is Morrison's last step.

concept: Lecture-cum-demonstration combines telling and showing
must_teach: Lecture-cum-demonstration: teacher explains a principle while demonstrating with apparatus/models; widely used in science; more concrete than pure lecture.

concept: Validity is the most important quality of a test
must_teach: Validity (measuring what it intends) is most important; reliability is necessary but not sufficient for validity; objectivity and usability are other qualities.

concept: Generic Elective: elective from an unrelated discipline in CBCS
must_teach: UGC CBCS: Core, Elective (Discipline Specific Elective from main discipline; Generic Elective from other discipline), Ability Enhancement Courses (AECC and Skill Enhancement Courses).

concept: Supportive administration aids teaching via freedom and resources
must_teach: Institutional leadership and climate are institution-related factors; supportive heads give freedom, resources and professional development, but do not replace planning, judgement or evaluation.

concept: Bobo doll experiment: observational learning (Bandura)
must_teach: Bandura's Bobo doll: children imitated an aggressive model; learning by observing models (social learning theory); trial and error = Thorndike; insight = Köhler; paired stimuli = Pavlov.

concept: Mock tests familiarise candidates with the CBT interface
must_teach: Mock tests in computer-based testing let candidates practise navigating, marking/changing answers and watching the timer; questions differ from the real exam.

concept: Smart classroom is equipped with digital teaching tools
must_teach: Smart classroom: computer, projector/interactive board, audio, internet for multimedia in face-to-face teaching; teacher remains central.

concept: DIKSHA is a digital platform for school education
must_teach: DIKSHA (Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing), launched 2017, NCERT-led under MoE: e-content for school students and teacher training; QR codes in textbooks.

concept: Adolescents are sensitive to criticism and peer opinion
must_teach: Adolescents are self-conscious, peer-sensitive, emotionally changeable and capable of abstract thought; correct them privately.

concept: Matching item: first-column entries are premises
must_teach: Matching items have premises (first column) and responses (second); more responses than premises reduces guessing; stem and distractors belong to MCQs.

concept: In Pavlov's experiment food is the unconditioned stimulus
must_teach: Pavlov: food = UCS, salivation to food = UCR, bell after pairing = CS, salivation to bell = CR.

concept: Imposing a fixed ideology is indoctrination, not a function of teaching
must_teach: Teaching transmits knowledge, develops skills, inculcates values while allowing reasoning; imposing unquestionable ideology is indoctrination.

concept: Teacher efficacy: belief in one's capacity to bring about learning
must_teach: Teacher efficacy = confidence in helping even difficult students learn; autonomy = professional freedom; accountability = answerability; burnout = exhaustion from stress.

concept: Evaluate is second-highest level of revised Bloom's taxonomy
must_teach: Revised order: Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyse, Evaluate, Create; Evaluate is fifth, below Create.

concept: In teacher-centred approach learner is a passive listener
must_teach: Teacher-centred: teacher controls content and pace, learners listen and take notes; discovering, joint planning and peer tutoring are learner-centred roles.

concept: Dyslexia mainly affects reading
must_teach: Dyslexia = reading/spelling difficulty; dyscalculia = calculation; dysgraphia = handwriting; dyspraxia = movement coordination.

concept: Analytic method moves from unknown to known
must_teach: Analytic method (maths) starts from what is to be found (unknown) and breaks it down to the given (known); synthetic method moves known to unknown and is shorter; maxim 'analysis to synthesis'.
flag: DOUBT: classic maxims list 'known to unknown' as a maxim; guide must distinguish the analytic method (unknown to known) from the maxim known-to-unknown to avoid confusing students. Outline has no clear home for analytic/synthetic methods (placed in 1.6).

concept: Reliability is expressed as a correlation coefficient
must_teach: Reliability is estimated by correlating two sets of scores (test-retest, split-half, parallel forms); coefficient ranges 0-1, about 0.80+ expected of standardised tests.

concept: Reflective level suits postgraduate and research students
must_teach: Reflective level needs knowledge base, mature reasoning and independence, so suits higher/PG/research classes; memory and understanding levels suit younger learners and beginners.

concept: Differentiated instruction adjusts content, process, product (Tomlinson)
must_teach: Differentiated instruction (Carol Ann Tomlinson): varying content, process and product by readiness, interest, learning profile; direct, programmed and mass instruction do not.

concept: Moodle is an open-source LMS
must_teach: Moodle (Modular Object-Oriented Dynamic Learning Environment) is free and open source; Blackboard is commercial; Google Classroom and MS Teams are proprietary.

concept: Flanders' Interaction Analysis studies classroom verbal interaction
must_teach: Flanders: ten categories, coded every three seconds (teacher talk, student talk, silence/confusion); shows direct vs indirect influence; verbal behaviour only.

concept: Maxim 'psychological to logical' starts from learner's interests and readiness
must_teach: Psychological order follows learner's interests, needs, development; logical order follows subject structure; teaching moves from former to latter.

concept: Buzz session: brief discussion in very small groups within a class
must_teach: Buzz session: large class split into groups of about 4-6 who discuss briefly and report back; brings participation into large classes.

concept: Effectiveness of teaching is judged by students' learning
must_teach: Teaching exists to produce learning; success measured by change in learners' knowledge, skills, attitudes, not lectures delivered, notes or silence.

concept: Teaching is a science because it follows testable principles
must_teach: Teaching as science: systematic principles of learning, motivation and evaluation that can be observed, tested and taught; as art: creative personal application.

concept: Egocentrism is typical of Piaget's pre-operational stage
must_teach: Pre-operational (2-7 yrs): egocentrism; reversibility appears in concrete operational; abstract reasoning and hypothesis testing in formal operational.

concept: Identifying unstated assumptions and organisation is Analyse (attributing, organising)
must_teach: Analyse = breaking material into parts and seeing relations; processes differentiating, organising, attributing; Evaluate needs judgement against criteria; Understand = explaining; Create = producing new.

concept: Essay tests excel at measuring organisation and expression of ideas
must_teach: Essay tests reveal ability to select, organise, integrate and express ideas; objective tests are superior in content sampling, scoring objectivity and speed of scoring.

concept: Flipped classroom: lower-order learning at home, higher-order in class
must_teach: Flipped classroom: first exposure (remember/understand) through videos/readings at home; applying, analysing, evaluating, creating in class with teacher and peers.

concept: Köhler's Sultan joining sticks illustrates insight learning
must_teach: Köhler (Gestalt): sudden solution by perceiving whole situation and relations = insight; trial and error = Thorndike; operant = Skinner; latent learning = Tolman.

concept: Merits and limits of lecture method
must_teach: Lecture suits large classes and can present material not in textbooks; it does not develop psychomotor skills and is largely one-way, so no feedback from every learner.

concept: Simpson's psychomotor taxonomy begins with Perception
must_teach: Simpson: perception, set, guided response, mechanism, complex overt response, adaptation, origination; Dave begins with imitation; Harrow with reflex movements; Receiving is affective.

concept: Absolute grading: fixed mark boundaries regardless of number of students
must_teach: Absolute grading fixes boundaries in marks in advance; relative grading (grading on the curve) sets boundaries by group performance, e.g. top 10% get A.

concept: Real-life survey with report and product is the project method
must_teach: Project method: purposeful real-life task with planning, execution, evaluation and tangible product; case study analyses an already written case; demonstration and tutorial differ.

concept: Weiner's attribution: effort is internal and unstable
must_teach: Weiner classifies causes by locus and stability: ability internal-stable, effort internal-unstable, task difficulty external-stable, luck external-unstable.

concept: Follow-up 'why do you think so?' is the skill of probing questioning
must_teach: Probing questioning: prompting, seeking clarification, refocusing, redirecting after a partial answer; reinforcement praises; explaining has teacher supply content; stimulus variation changes cues.

concept: Knowles's andragogical assumptions about adult learners
must_teach: Knowles's assumptions: need to know, self-concept, experience, readiness linked to social roles, problem-/life-centred orientation, internal motivation; subject-centred orientation is pedagogy.

concept: Test anxiety is an emotional learner-related factor
must_teach: Learner factors include cognitive, physical, emotional and social; anxiety is emotional and consumes attention and working memory; institutional factors lie outside the learner.

concept: Classification and seriation without hypothetical reasoning = concrete operational stage
must_teach: Concrete operational (about 7-11): classification, seriation, conservation on real objects; hypothetical-deductive reasoning needs formal operations; age is only a rough guide.

concept: Converting text to a graph is translation, a form of Comprehension
must_teach: Bloom 1956 Comprehension has three forms: translation, interpretation, extrapolation; changing words to a graph is translation, not Application or Analysis.

concept: In computer adaptive testing next item depends on earlier responses
must_teach: CAT estimates ability as it proceeds: correct answer brings harder item, wrong answer easier; precise score with fewer items.

concept: Reflective level task: weigh conflicting evidence and defend a solution
must_teach: Reflective level needs a genuine problem; learners weigh evidence and defend their conclusions; explaining in own words and using taught formula = understanding; listing = memory.

concept: Observing cases before stating the law follows 'particular to general'
must_teach: Maxim 'particular to general' underlies inductive method; stating the law first then verifying = 'general to particular' (deductive).

concept: In Kolb's cycle reflective observation follows concrete experience
must_teach: Kolb's cycle: concrete experience, reflective observation, abstract conceptualisation, active experimentation; styles diverging, assimilating, converging, accommodating.

concept: Facility value 0.90 means a very easy item
must_teach: Difficulty index/facility value = proportion answering correctly; 0.90 = very easy; items near 0.50 discriminate best; very easy or hard items discriminate poorly.

concept: Memory-level objective suits drill with recall-type test
must_teach: Reproducing facts is a memory-level outcome; drill and repetition fix facts; recall/recognition items test them; seminars, projects, debates aim higher.

concept: Indian micro-teaching cycle totals 36 minutes
must_teach: Indian model (Passi): teach 6, feedback 6, re-plan 12, re-teach 6, re-feedback 6 minutes = 36 minutes; peers as pupils.

concept: Bruner's spiral curriculum revisits key ideas at rising complexity
must_teach: Bruner: any subject can be taught in honest form at any stage; curriculum returns to basic ideas at higher levels; enactive, iconic, symbolic modes.

concept: Action verbs mapped to revised Bloom levels
must_teach: Summarise = Understand; Differentiate = Analyse; Justify = Evaluate; Compose = Create.

concept: Operations of pre-active, interactive and post-active phases
must_teach: Pre-active: fixing objectives, selecting and sequencing content, planning; interactive: presenting stimuli, feedback, reinforcement; post-active: choosing testing devices, evaluating outcomes.

concept: Gifted learners need enrichment through challenging tasks
must_teach: Provisions for gifted: enrichment, acceleration, independent projects, mentoring; repetition increases boredom; exemption wastes ability.

concept: Distinguishing seminar, symposium, panel discussion and workshop
must_teach: Seminar: paper presented then discussed in depth; symposium: successive prepared talks on aspects of a theme; panel: moderated informal conversation of experts before audience; workshop: hands-on production under resource persons.

concept: cMOOCs are connectivist, network-based MOOCs
must_teach: cMOOCs (Siemens and Downes, connectivism) rely on learner networks; xMOOCs are structured instructor-led platform courses; SPOC = small private online course.

concept: Norm-referenced interpretation compares with a group (percentile)
must_teach: Norm-referenced: position relative to group (e.g. higher than 85% of class); criterion-referenced: performance against fixed task/standard.

concept: Withholding reinforcement so behaviour dies out is extinction
must_teach: Extinction: behaviour weakens when its reinforcer is withheld; punishment applies something unpleasant or removes pleasant; negative reinforcement removes aversive to strengthen behaviour; spontaneous recovery is reappearance after extinction.

concept: Aim of classroom management is maximising learning time
must_teach: Classroom management organises space, time, routines and relationships to maximise engaged learning time and prevent problems; not punishment or silence.

concept: Order of Krathwohl's affective domain levels
must_teach: Affective order: Receiving, Responding, Valuing, Organisation, Characterisation (by a value complex); principle of internalisation.

concept: Video conferencing allows live two-way interaction across sites
must_teach: Video conferencing gives synchronous two-way audio-video among several places; podcasts and screen recordings are one-way asynchronous; e-mail lacks immediacy.

concept: Support material is best when relevant and used at the right moment
must_teach: Aids are means not ends: chosen for the objective, accurate, visible, shown when needed and removed after; too many or constantly displayed aids distract.

concept: Jigsaw: each member masters one part and teaches it to group
must_teach: Aronson's jigsaw: home groups, each member gets one part, expert groups study same part, return to teach home group; positive interdependence.

concept: Performance assessment reveals skills but is slower and more subjective to score
must_teach: Performance-based tasks show what students can actually do; they take longer to mark and depend on assessor judgement, hence rubrics; MCQs are quicker and more objective.

concept: Elkind's imaginary audience: belief that others constantly watch
must_teach: Elkind's adolescent egocentrism: imaginary audience (being always on stage, self-consciousness) and personal fable (uniqueness, invulnerability, risk-taking).

concept: Teacher's non-verbal behaviour affects learning because students read it as message
must_teach: Classroom communication is carried by voice, face, gesture, eye contact and movement; learners read these cues, so non-verbal behaviour influences learning.

concept: Purpose, not instrument, makes evaluation formative or summative
must_teach: A test used to locate weaknesses for re-teaching is formative; term-end exam deciding promotion is summative.

concept: Debriefing/discussion after role play is key for learning
must_teach: Role play enactment provides experience; learning comes from discussion/debriefing by players and observers linking it to objectives.

concept: From memory to reflective level, teacher control falls and learner participation rises
must_teach: Memory level: teacher dominant, learner passive; understanding: more participation; reflective: learners lead inquiry, teacher guides.

concept: Epidiascope projects opaque objects and transparent slides
must_teach: Epidiascope = episcope (opaque material by reflected light) + diascope (transparent slides); projected visual aid needing darkened room.

concept: Pre-test is diagnostic and remedial worksheets prescriptive function of teaching
must_teach: Functions of teaching: diagnostic (finding entry behaviour and weaknesses), prescriptive (choosing content/activities to remedy), evaluative (checking outcomes).

concept: Checking each answer immediately is the principle of immediate confirmation
must_teach: Programmed instruction principles: small steps, active responding, immediate confirmation (feedback), self-pacing, student testing (Skinner).

concept: Knowing the learner: adjusting examples and pace after gauging prior knowledge
must_teach: Basic requirement 'knowing the learner' = finding out prior knowledge, differences and needs and fitting the lesson; finishing early, dictating notes, hard papers do not show it.

concept: CBCS AECC = Environmental Science and English/MIL Communication
must_teach: UGC CBCS (2015): Ability Enhancement Compulsory Courses are Environmental Science and English/MIL Communication; Skill Enhancement Courses are skill/value based; core and electives separate.
flag: DATED: reflects UGC CBCS 2015 guidelines; CCFUP 2022 renames categories (AEC, SEC, VAC) - guide should present 2015 scheme as the CBCS answer and note the newer framework.

concept: Investigating cause of a persistent specific error is diagnostic evaluation
must_teach: Diagnostic evaluation seeks causes of persistent learning difficulties and leads to remedial teaching; formative only shows weakness; placement is at entry; summative at end.

concept: Morrison insists on mastery; recitation is oral presentation in own words
must_teach: Morrison's mastery formula: pre-test, teach, test, adapt, teach and test to actual learning; recitation = pupil presents organised unit in own words, not verbatim.

concept: Sensing others' moods and teamwork = Gardner's interpersonal intelligence
must_teach: Interpersonal = understanding others' feelings, motives; intrapersonal = understanding oneself; linguistic = language; naturalistic = nature classification.

concept: NPTEL, Shodhganga, Virtual Labs and NDLI descriptions
must_teach: NPTEL: online courses by IITs and IISc; Shodhganga (INFLIBNET): repository of Indian theses; Virtual Labs: simulated web experiments; NDLI (IIT Kharagpur): single-window search for learning resources.

concept: Continuum: conditioning, training, instruction, teaching
must_teach: Conditioning links response to stimulus; training builds skill through practice; instruction imparts organised knowledge; teaching aims at understanding, reasoning and values.

concept: Rotation model of blended learning: scheduled movement between online and teacher-led stations
must_teach: Blended learning models (Christensen Institute): rotation (move on schedule between online and other modes, e.g. station rotation), flex (online backbone), enriched virtual (mostly remote), self-blend/a la carte (student adds online courses).

concept: Chalkboard limitation: teacher's back turned to class while writing
must_teach: Chalkboard: cheap, always available, needs no power, diagrams grow step by step; limits: loss of eye contact while writing, content rubbed off and not stored.

concept: Blueprint: two-way table of content units and objectives before writing a test
must_teach: Blueprint/table of specifications relates content to objectives (and question forms), ensuring proportional sampling and content validity; marking scheme and scoring key come after items are written.

concept: Prior knowledge and fatigue are learner-related factors
must_teach: New material is interpreted through prior knowledge (Ausubel); physical condition such as fatigue reduces attention and efficiency of learning.

concept: Herbartian comparison/association links new material to earlier ideas (apperception)
must_teach: Herbart's apperception: new ideas learnt by linking to existing apperceptive mass; comparison/association step connects new facts with old; preparation tests prior knowledge and states aim; application uses rule on fresh examples.

concept: Flanders' observer records a category every 3 seconds
must_teach: Flanders: category recorded every three seconds (about 20 a minute), entered in a 10x10 matrix to compute teacher talk, student talk, indirect/direct ratios.

concept: Understanding-level test item: explain a principle and apply to familiar example
must_teach: Understanding level: seeing relationships, explaining in own words, applying principles in familiar situations; exact reproduction/recitation = memory; original theory = reflective.

concept: CGPA is credit-weighted mean of SGPAs
must_teach: CGPA = sum(credits x SGPA)/total credits; (20x7 + 30x8)/50 = 380/50 = 7.6; simple average 7.5 is wrong.

concept: Teaching is purposeful because directed to predetermined objectives
must_teach: Teaching is a purposeful/goal-directed activity aimed at desired changes in learners; without objectives an activity is not teaching.

concept: Visualising a building from a plan is Gardner's spatial intelligence
must_teach: Spatial intelligence: perceiving and mentally transforming the visual world (architects, sculptors, navigators, chess); bodily-kinaesthetic = skilled body use; logical-mathematical = reasoning, numbers; naturalistic = classifying nature.

concept: Remote proctoring: supervising candidates via webcam and screen monitoring
must_teach: Remote proctoring supervises online test-takers at their own location via webcam, microphone and screen monitoring (software or human), verifying identity and flagging suspicious behaviour.

concept: Andragogy favours case discussion drawing on participants' experience
must_teach: Andragogy uses learners' experience as a resource and problem-centred participatory methods (case discussion); dictation, drill and lecture-recall treat learners as dependent receivers.

concept: CBT lets candidates change answers any number of times before submitting
must_teach: In CBT answers can be changed, cleared or marked for review until submission and a question palette shows unanswered items; OMR marks cannot be altered; CBT needs power and does not allow choosing difficulty.

concept: Mixed-ability classes: flexible grouping and graded assignments
must_teach: Individual differences are met by flexible grouping and graded/tiered assignments; uniform lecture, pace and homework ignore readiness differences; public ranking harms.

concept: Giving a formula then applying to problems is the deductive method
must_teach: Deductive: general rule first then particular cases (quick, practice, less discovery); inductive: from examples to rule; heuristic: learner discovers; analytic: unknown to known.

concept: Evaluation adds value judgement to measurement
must_teach: Measurement reports quantities (marks, items correct, time); evaluation interprets and judges worth (e.g. 'shows very good progress'); evaluation = measurement + value judgement.
flag: WRONG?: explanation says 'the first statement interprets a score' but the key (C) is the third option; wording of the explanation is inconsistent with the key and should read 'option (C)'.

concept: CBCS ten-point scale grade O = Outstanding
must_teach: UGC ten-point scale: O Outstanding 10, A+ Excellent 9, A Very Good 8, B+ Good 7, B Above Average 6, C Average 5, P Pass 4, F Fail 0, Ab Absent 0.

concept: Facilities help only when teachers are trained and willing to use them
must_teach: Instructional facilities are enabling conditions; their effect depends on teacher skill and readiness, so institutions must give training and support along with equipment.

concept: Returning drafts with comments is formative assessment
must_teach: Formative assessment guides ongoing learning (feedback on drafts); final results, scholarship ranking and entrance tests are decision-making (summative/selection/placement) uses.

concept: Forum posts at different times are asynchronous learning
must_teach: Asynchronous: participants contribute at different times (forums, e-mail, recorded lectures), allowing reflection; synchronous requires simultaneous presence (live class).

concept: Task solvable only with hints lies within the zone of proximal development
must_teach: Vygotsky: actual development = unaided performance; ZPD = what can be done with guidance; beyond ZPD = not even with help; instruction most fruitful in ZPD.

concept: Equilibration balances assimilation and accommodation (Piaget)
must_teach: Equilibration is Piaget's self-regulating process resolving disequilibrium through assimilation and accommodation; conservation, seriation and centration are stage features.

concept: Personalised System of Instruction (Keller Plan) is by Fred Keller
must_teach: Fred S. Keller's PSI: self-paced units from written material, unit mastery shown by test with student proctor, lectures only to motivate; Skinner = linear programming; Crowder = branching; Bloom = mastery learning.
flag: DOUBT: outline lists personalised system of instruction in 4.2 but Keller Plan in 4.4; guide should treat PSI and Keller Plan in one place.

concept: Rigid exam-driven curriculum narrows teaching to the test
must_teach: When everything depends on final exams, teaching narrows to likely questions ('teaching to the test'), an institution-related constraint on methods.

concept: Adding good-quality items generally increases reliability
must_teach: Longer tests sample ability more fully so chance errors cancel; Spearman-Brown formula relates test length and reliability; very short tests are unreliable.

concept: Levels of teaching are cumulative: understanding includes memory; reflective needs both
must_teach: Memory, understanding and reflective levels are hierarchical and cumulative; reflection presupposes facts and understanding, so it cannot dispense with memory level.

concept: Effective demonstration: every student can see and hear each step
must_teach: Demonstration needs visibility and audibility, rehearsal, step-by-step moderate pace, simple apparatus and questioning during it.

concept: Complicated language in a maths test threatens validity
must_teach: When reading ability affects scores in a maths test, something other than the intended ability is measured, lowering validity even if scoring stays objective.

concept: Concept Attainment Model is in the information-processing family
must_teach: Joyce & Weil: Concept Attainment (Bruner), Inquiry Training (Suchman), Advance Organiser (Ausubel) belong to information-processing family; other families social, personal, behavioural systems.

concept: Approval and law-and-order reasoning is Kohlberg's conventional level
must_teach: Kohlberg: pre-conventional (punishment, reward), conventional (good boy/girl approval; law and order), post-conventional (social contract, universal principles).

concept: Judging two designs against criteria and recommending one is Evaluate
must_teach: Evaluate = judgements based on criteria (checking, critiquing); Create = producing new; Analyse = breaking into parts; Apply = executing procedures.

concept: Project, problem-solving and group discussion are learner-centred; dictation is teacher-centred
must_teach: Learner-centred methods make the learner the chief actor (project, problem-solving, discussion); dictation is teacher-controlled.

concept: Good teaching gives feedback and links to prior knowledge; it is flexible
must_teach: Good teaching provides feedback, links new to known, is flexible to learner responses, and is judged by learning not content coverage.

concept: Herzberg: salary and working conditions are hygiene factors
must_teach: Herzberg's two-factor theory: hygiene factors (salary, security, supervision, conditions) prevent dissatisfaction; motivators (achievement, recognition, responsibility, work itself) produce satisfaction.

concept: Breaking into clauses then building new sentences follows 'analysis to synthesis'
must_teach: Maxim 'analysis to synthesis': separate whole into elements to understand, then recombine into meaningful whole; learning incomplete without synthesis.

concept: NPTEL is SWAYAM national coordinator for engineering
must_teach: SWAYAM national coordinators: NPTEL engineering; CEC non-technology UG; UGC non-technology PG; IGNOU out-of-school/diploma; NCERT and NIOS school; IIMB management; NITTTR teacher training; AICTE for self-paced/international courses.
flag: DATED: list of SWAYAM national coordinators (count and roles) changes over time - verify current list on swayam.gov.in.

concept: VARK preferences matched to suitable activities
must_teach: Fleming's VARK: Visual - diagrams, flow charts; Aural - listening, discussion; Read/Write - lists, notes; Kinaesthetic - practice, field experiments.

concept: Gagné's hierarchy order: signal, ..., concept, rule, problem solving
must_teach: Gagné's eight types: signal, stimulus-response, chaining, verbal association, discrimination, concept, rule (principle), problem solving; each prerequisite for the next.

concept: NRT items spread scores; CRT reports mastery; easy CRT items need not be discarded
must_teach: NRT selects middle-difficulty discriminating items to spread scores; CRT reports mastery/non-mastery against a standard; in CRT an item all answer correctly can show teaching success.

concept: Accurate independent performance with attention is Dave's precision level
must_teach: Dave: imitation (copying model), manipulation (following instructions), precision (accurate, independent), articulation (coordinating sequence), naturalisation (automatic).

concept: Multimedia integrates text, graphics, audio, video and animation
must_teach: Multimedia combines text, images, sound, video and animation, usually computer-controlled and interactive; addresses several senses.

concept: Reflective level needs a climate permitting free questioning
must_teach: Reflective level needs an open democratic climate where learners can doubt, question, propose and test ideas; fixed sequences or imposed answers leave nothing to reflect on.

concept: Instructional objectives describe learner behaviour with conditions and criterion
must_teach: Well-written objectives: stated from learner's side, observable verbs (list, explain, solve), conditions and criterion (Mager); vague verbs like know, understand, appreciate are not measurable.

concept: On-the-spot decision during lesson belongs to interactive phase (Jackson)
must_teach: Jackson: pre-active = deliberate planning; interactive = spontaneous decisions while facing class; post-active = reflection and evaluation after teaching.

concept: Project method by Kilpatrick; hard to use alone for a syllabus
must_teach: Project method (W.H. Kilpatrick, Dewey's pragmatism) is time-consuming and gives incidental, unsystematic knowledge, so hard as sole method; propounder is unrelated reason.

concept: Direct grading assigns grades without first awarding marks
must_teach: Direct grading: qualitative judgement straight into grades; indirect grading: marks first then converted by fixed ranges (absolute) or group position (relative).

concept: Cognitive domain ordered by increasing complexity
must_teach: Organising principles: cognitive - complexity; affective - internalisation; psychomotor - coordination.

concept: Praise after every fifth correct answer is fixed-ratio schedule
must_teach: Ratio schedules depend on number of responses, interval schedules on time; fixed-ratio = set number; variable-ratio = varying number around average; fixed/variable interval by time.

concept: Rapporteur records proceedings and prepares report
must_teach: Rapporteur records and reports proceedings; convener organises; chairperson/moderator conducts; discussant critiques a paper.

concept: Favouring tuition students in marks violates impartiality
must_teach: Professional ethics require just, impartial treatment of all students especially in assessment and discourage private tuition creating conflict of interest.

concept: Language laboratory is for listening and speaking practice
must_teach: Language lab: audio/computer stations where learners listen to model speech, record and compare responses with teacher monitoring; for oral-aural skills.

concept: Instruction can occur without a teacher; indoctrination discourages critical examination
must_teach: Instruction can be delivered by programmed texts, computers, broadcasts without a teacher present; indoctrination presents beliefs as unquestionable.

concept: Podcast: downloadable on-demand audio episodes
must_teach: Podcast = audio/video files over internet for on-demand (asynchronous) listening; webinar = live online seminar; blog = web journal; wiki = collaboratively edited site.

concept: Herbartian preparation step recalls prior knowledge and states aim
must_teach: Preparation/introduction recalls related previous knowledge, arouses curiosity, ends with statement of aim; followed by presentation, comparison, generalisation, application.

concept: Handouts give an outline that reduces note-taking burden
must_teach: Good handouts give structure, key terms, diagrams so students listen and think; they support but do not replace lecture or further reading.

concept: RCEM approach to objectives developed at Regional College of Education, Mysore
must_teach: RCEM = Regional College of Education Mysore approach: objectives in categories knowledge, understanding, application, creativity, stated through specified mental processes instead of action verbs.
flag: DOUBT: explanation says RCEM specifies seventeen mental processes; sources vary on the count - verify before the guide states a number.

concept: CEC is an inter-university centre of the UGC
must_teach: CEC (Consortium for Educational Communication), New Delhi: UGC inter-university centre for electronic media; coordinates EMRCs; national coordinator for SWAYAM (UG non-technology) and SWAYAM PRABHA.

concept: Mastery learning formative tests identify unmastered objectives for correctives
must_teach: Bloom's mastery learning: unit formative tests (ungraded) reveal unmastered objectives; correctives and second test follow; grading by later summative test.

concept: Team teaching: two or more teachers jointly plan, teach and evaluate a group
must_teach: Team teaching: teachers pool strengths and share planning, teaching and evaluation of the same students; peer tutoring is students teaching each other.

concept: Syntax of a teaching model is the sequence of phases
must_teach: Joyce and Weil model elements: focus, syntax (phases), social system (roles, relationships), principles of reaction (teacher responses), support system (materials).

concept: Overview comparing new with familiar topic is a comparative advance organiser
must_teach: Ausubel: comparative organiser relates new material to familiar knowledge (similarities, differences); expository organiser gives framework for wholly new material.

concept: In simulated teaching trainee rotates teacher, pupil and observer roles
must_teach: Simulated teaching: small group of trainees practise among themselves, one teaches, others act as pupils and observers, roles rotated.

concept: Order of Bandura's observational learning processes
must_teach: Bandura: attention, retention, reproduction (motor), motivation; reinforcement (direct or vicarious) mainly affects motivation.

concept: At reflective level hypotheses are formed and tested by learners
must_teach: Reflective level follows inquiry: problem recognised, learners propose and test hypotheses, weigh evidence; teacher sharpens problem but does not supply hypotheses or conclusions.

concept: Appreciation and respect objectives belong to affective domain
must_teach: Affective = feelings, attitudes, values (appreciates, shows respect); cognitive = intellectual (solves equations); psychomotor = manual skill (operates microscope).

concept: SWAYAM four quadrants include online discussion forum
must_teach: SWAYAM four quadrants: e-tutorial (video lectures), e-content (reading material), self-assessment (quizzes/tests), discussion forum.

concept: Teacher expectations and questioning skill affect learning; subject knowledge alone is insufficient
must_teach: Teacher expectations work as self-fulfilling prophecy (Pygmalion); questioning skill affects participation; subject knowledge is necessary but not sufficient.

concept: Low completion rate is a reported limitation of MOOCs
must_teach: MOOCs are open, free, unlimited enrolment, video-centred; low completion due to lack of personal contact, self-discipline, incentives.

concept: Completion and short-answer items are supply-type items
must_teach: Objective items: supply-type/recall (completion, short-answer) vs selection-type/recognition (true-false, matching, MCQ).

concept: Discrimination index = (RU - RL) / size of one group
must_teach: DI = (upper correct - lower correct)/n per group: (32-12)/40 = 0.50; dividing by 80 gives 0.25 (error); facility value = 44/80 = 0.55.

concept: Lewin, Lippitt and White: democratic leadership gave good work and highest morale
must_teach: Authoritarian: hard work only under watch, hostility; laissez-faire: little work; democratic: work continued in leader's absence, friendly and satisfied members.

concept: Learning through hands-on action is Bruner's enactive mode
must_teach: Bruner's modes: enactive (action), iconic (images, diagrams), symbolic (words, formulae), recommended in that order.

concept: Hearing-impaired learners benefit from captions and written outlines
must_teach: Hearing impairment: visual channels - captions, written outlines, visual aids, front seat for lip-reading, sign language; Braille/large print serve visual impairment.

concept: Peer assessment reliability improved by clear rubrics and anonymous marking
must_teach: Peer marks distorted by friendship, rivalry, vague standards; rubrics, anonymity, multiple markers averaged, and training with samples improve reliability.

concept: Guilford's structure-of-intellect dimensions: operations, contents, products
must_teach: Guilford's SI model: operations (e.g. memory, divergent production), contents (e.g. symbolic, semantic), products (e.g. units, relations); 120 or more abilities; Sternberg = analytical/creative/practical; Cattell = fluid/crystallised.

concept: Individual accountability prevents free riding in cooperative learning
must_teach: Johnson and Johnson essentials: positive interdependence, individual accountability, face-to-face (promotive) interaction, social skills, group processing.

concept: Pedagogy assumes dependent learner; andragogy self-directing learner
must_teach: Knowles: pedagogy - dependent learner, subject-centred, external motivation; andragogy - self-directing, problem-centred, internal motivation.

concept: Scores from multi-shift CBT are equated through normalisation
must_teach: Different shift papers differ in difficulty, so raw scores are normalised (usually to percentile scores); randomisation only shuffles items; negative marking and revaluation do not equate.

concept: Shulman's pedagogical content knowledge: making a subject comprehensible
must_teach: Shulman's PCK: blend of content and pedagogy - best examples, analogies, explanations for a topic and typical learner difficulties; distinct from subject knowledge and general skill.

concept: Robert Glaser introduced criterion-referenced measurement (1963)
must_teach: Glaser (1963) distinguished norm- and criterion-referenced measurement in programmed instruction context; Scriven coined formative/summative evaluation.

concept: Commitment without exploration is Marcia's identity foreclosure
must_teach: Marcia's statuses: diffusion (no exploration, no commitment), foreclosure (commitment without exploration), moratorium (exploration without commitment), achievement (commitment after exploration).

concept: Knowledge and Comprehension are lower-order levels of Bloom
must_teach: Lower-order: Knowledge, Comprehension, Application; higher-order: Analysis, Synthesis, Evaluation.

concept: Purposes of placement, formative, diagnostic and summative evaluation
must_teach: Placement: entry behaviour before instruction; formative: monitor progress, feedback; diagnostic: causes of persistent difficulties; summative: certify achievement at end.

concept: On UGC ten-point scale B+ (Good) = 7
must_teach: UGC scale: O 10, A+ 9, A 8, B+ 7, B 6, C 5, P 4, F 0.

concept: Memory level is retained in higher education as base for higher levels; linked to Herbart
must_teach: Higher levels need a base of facts, so memory-level teaching is not discarded; memory level is associated with Herbart (true but unrelated reason).

concept: Evaluative function of teaching: checking achievement of objectives after a unit
must_teach: Functions of teaching: diagnostic (entry behaviour), prescriptive (choosing strategy and aids), evaluative (judging outcomes against objectives and improving teaching).

concept: In Dale's Cone, visual symbols are more abstract than motion pictures
must_teach: Dale's Cone bottom to top: direct experiences, contrived experiences, dramatised experiences, demonstrations, study trips, exhibits, (TV), motion pictures, recordings/radio/still pictures, visual symbols, verbal symbols.

concept: Assessment gathers and interprets evidence; evaluation judges worth
must_teach: Assessment collects evidence (tests, observation, assignments) and interprets it; evaluation judges worth against objectives or standards and includes assessment.

concept: Resolving value conflicts into consistent priorities is affective Organisation
must_teach: Organisation: bringing values together, resolving conflicts, building consistent value system; Valuing concerns single value; Characterisation = value system controls behaviour consistently over time.

concept: Self-determination theory needs: autonomy, competence, relatedness
must_teach: Deci and Ryan SDT: autonomy, competence, relatedness; Maslow: safety, belonging, esteem; McClelland: achievement, power, affiliation; Alderfer ERG: existence, relatedness, growth.

concept: Link practice integrates micro-teaching skills before real teaching
must_teach: Micro-teaching trains one skill at a time; link practice (integration of skills) combines skills in intermediate-length lessons with intermediate groups before real classroom.

concept: Witkin's field-independent learners are analytical and work well alone
must_teach: Witkin: field-independent learners separate items from background, analytical, self-directed; field-dependent learners perceive globally, attend to social cues, prefer group work and guidance.

concept: 'Practice makes perfect' expresses Thorndike's law of exercise
must_teach: Thorndike's laws: readiness, exercise (use strengthens, disuse weakens), effect (satisfying consequences strengthen); belongingness is a later subsidiary law; exercise later qualified by knowledge of results.

concept: Lecture is economical because one teacher reaches many students
must_teach: Lecture economy: high learner-teacher ratio and much content per hour, so low cost and time per student.

concept: Single paper presented, discussant comments, open discussion = seminar
must_teach: Seminar: one paper presented and examined in depth (discussant, chairperson); symposium: several speakers on aspects of theme; panel: expert conversation; workshop: practical work.

concept: Components of set induction, stimulus variation, reinforcement and closure
must_teach: Set induction links with previous knowledge; stimulus variation shifts sensory channels; reinforcement uses praise and nods; closure summarises main points.

concept: Knowing steps of a statistical test is procedural knowledge
must_teach: Revised taxonomy knowledge dimension: factual (terms, details), conceptual (classifications, principles, theories), procedural (methods, techniques, algorithms), metacognitive (awareness of own thinking).

concept: Appreciation project is Kilpatrick's consumer (aesthetic) project
must_teach: Kilpatrick's four project types: producer/constructive (make something), consumer/aesthetic (enjoyment, appreciation), problem (intellectual question), drill (mastering skill/knowledge).

concept: Visiting a fort before discussing feudalism follows 'concrete to abstract'
must_teach: Maxim 'concrete to abstract': give tangible experience first, then build abstract concept; starting with definition reverses it.

concept: Understanding level still depends largely on teacher's explanation
must_teach: Understanding level: teacher explains relationships and learner grasps them, thinking largely teacher's; no originality demanded; builds on relationships and prior knowledge and can be tested.

concept: Herbart's apperception: new ideas linked to existing apperceptive mass
must_teach: Herbart: mind is an apperceptive mass; learning assimilates new ideas into it; formal steps secure linkage; connectionism = Thorndike; equilibration = Piaget.

concept: Teacher-centred to learner-centred = transmitting content to facilitating knowledge construction
must_teach: Learner-centred approach: learner constructs knowledge through activity, teacher designs and guides; continuous assessment and cooperation are learner-centred features.

concept: Debate: two teams argue for and against a motion under rules
must_teach: Debate: motion, two opposing sides, fixed speaker order, time limits; panel exchanges views without fixed sides; symposium presents aspects of theme; colloquium is an academic discussion meeting.

concept: Piaget: fixed stage order, pre-operational egocentrism, active child, formal operations at ~11
must_teach: Piaget's stage sequence is invariant (ages vary); egocentrism marks pre-operational; child is active constructor; formal operations begin about 11-12 years.

concept: Belief that results depend on own effort = internal locus of control (Rotter)
must_teach: Rotter's locus of control: internal (own effort, responsibility, persistence) vs external (luck, others); learned helplessness = belief nothing one does matters.

concept: Essay tests have low scorer reliability and sample the syllabus narrowly
must_teach: Essay marks vary across examiners (judgement-dependent scoring); essays have few questions so sample narrowly; objective tests sample widely.

concept: Flanders: two categories for student talk
must_teach: Flanders: categories 1-7 teacher talk (1-4 indirect, 5-7 direct), 8-9 student talk (response, initiation), 10 silence/confusion.

concept: Sound film appeals to both ear and eye (audio-visual aid)
must_teach: Audio aids: tape recorder, radio; visual aids: filmstrip, flannel board, charts; audio-visual: sound film, television; more senses usually aid retention.

concept: Morrison defined teaching as intimate contact between mature and less mature personality
must_teach: Morrison (1934): intimate contact of more mature and less mature personality; Gage: interpersonal influence; B.O. Smith: system of actions to induce learning; Amidon: interactive process of classroom talk.

concept: Wiki supports collaborative writing and editing of web pages
must_teach: Wiki: pages any authorised user creates/edits via browser with change history; podcasts, webcasts, screencasts are one-to-many audio/video delivery.

concept: Teacher as independent variable plans, organises and manipulates teaching
must_teach: Teaching variables: teacher = independent (manipulates process), learner = dependent (behaviour changes), content/method/environment = intervening.

concept: Formative evaluation results modify instruction still in progress
must_teach: Formative evaluation defined by use: findings improve ongoing teaching and learning; external setting, whole-course coverage and final grades typify summative.

concept: Break a lecture with an activity about every 15-20 minutes
must_teach: Attention is high at the start of a lecture and is commonly said to decline after about 15-20 minutes; lectures should be segmented with questions, tasks or change of medium.
flag: DOUBT: the 15-20 minute attention-span claim is widely taught but its research basis is contested (e.g. Wilson & Korn 2007; Bradbury 2016); guide may present it as conventional advice.

concept: Kolb's converger combines abstract conceptualisation and active experimentation
must_teach: Kolb styles: converger (AC+AE, practical application), diverger (CE+RO, imaginative), assimilator (AC+RO, theory building), accommodator (CE+AE, hands-on, intuitive).

concept: Classical IQ = (MA / CA) x 100
must_teach: IQ = mental age / chronological age x 100; MA 12, CA 10 gives 120; inverting gives about 83; IQ 100 means MA = CA.

concept: Evaluation process: objectives, learning experiences, tools, interpretation
must_teach: Evaluation starts with formulating objectives, then providing learning experiences, applying evaluation tools, interpreting results; objectives-learning experiences-evaluation triangle.

concept: Using a preferred activity to reinforce a less preferred one = Premack principle
must_teach: Premack principle ('Grandma's rule'): high-frequency behaviour reinforces low-frequency behaviour; shaping = successive approximations; token economy = exchangeable tokens.

concept: Harrow's psychomotor taxonomy tops with non-discursive communication
must_teach: Harrow: reflex movements, basic fundamental movements, perceptual abilities, physical abilities, skilled movements, non-discursive communication; Simpson tops with origination, Dave with naturalisation; characterisation is affective.

concept: Holistic rubric gives one overall score
must_teach: Holistic rubric: describes overall quality levels, single score, quick but little diagnostic feedback; analytic rubric scores each criterion separately; checklist lists features present/absent.

concept: Blended learning retains face-to-face interaction while adding online flexibility
must_teach: Blended learning keeps classroom social presence, immediate feedback and practical work and adds online flexibility and self-pacing; still needs campus, devices and careful planning.

concept: Skinner's linear programming uses small steps to keep error rate low
must_teach: Skinner's linear programme: small steps so responses are almost always correct and reinforced; Crowder's branching programme uses errors for diagnosis.

concept: Induction is slower; deduction suits practice and revision of established rules
must_teach: Inductive method is slow (many examples before rule) but promotes discovery; deductive is quick (rule given) and suits application, practice, revision.

concept: SGPA as credit-weighted average of grade points
must_teach: SGPA = sum(credits x grade point)/total credits: (36+28+10)/10 = 7.4; simple average 7.0 is wrong.

concept: Matching maxims with classroom practices
must_teach: Simple to complex: simple before compound sentences; concrete to abstract: beads before number symbols; whole to part: whole poem before stanzas; particular to general: measured triangles before angle-sum rule.

concept: Affective domain ordered by internalisation
must_teach: Krathwohl's affective levels ordered by internalisation (Receiving to Characterisation); cognitive by complexity; psychomotor by coordination.

concept: Overjustification effect: extrinsic reward undermines intrinsic interest
must_teach: Overjustification: rewarding an already enjoyed activity shifts the reason to reward, so interest falls below baseline when reward stops; Hawthorne = being observed; Pygmalion = expectations; Zeigarnik = memory for unfinished tasks.

concept: Levels of teaching differ in amount of thinking demanded (Bigge)
must_teach: Bigge: continuum from thoughtless to thoughtful teaching; memory least thought, understanding more, reflective most; not defined by time, class size or teacher age.

concept: Gagné's nine events of instruction begin with gaining attention
must_teach: Gagné's nine events: gain attention, inform objective, stimulate recall, present stimulus, provide guidance, elicit performance, give feedback, assess performance, enhance retention and transfer.

concept: Universal Design for Learning: multiple means of representation, engagement, expression
must_teach: UDL (CAST) plans variety from the start - multiple means of representation, engagement and action/expression - benefiting all and reducing later accommodation; not segregation or uniform method.

concept: Revised Bloom's two dimensions: knowledge and cognitive process
must_teach: Anderson and Krathwohl taxonomy table: knowledge dimension (factual, conceptual, procedural, metacognitive) x cognitive process dimension (Remember to Create).

concept: Credit transfer: credits earned at one institution accepted by another
must_teach: CBCS expresses courses in credits on a common pattern so credits earned can be counted at another institution, enabling mobility (now via Academic Bank of Credits).

concept: Heavy non-teaching duties reduce time for preparation and students
must_teach: Workload is an institution-related factor; clerical/administrative duties take time from preparation, feedback and student contact and add fatigue.

concept: Item everyone answers correctly has little value in an NRT as it does not discriminate
must_teach: NRT ranks examinees, so items answered correctly or wrongly by all add nothing and are dropped; in CRT they may be retained.

concept: Havighurst proposed developmental tasks
must_teach: Havighurst: developmental tasks society expects at each stage; adolescence tasks include accepting one's body, emotional independence, mature peer relations, career preparation; Erikson: psychosocial stages; Hall: storm and stress.

concept: 'Whole is more than sum of parts' is Gestalt principle
must_teach: Gestalt psychology (Wertheimer, Köhler, Koffka): perceiving and learning organised wholes, insight; behaviourism and connectionism analyse into S-R units; structuralism analyses consciousness into elements.

concept: Reflective level evaluated by essay tests and needs open, free climate
must_teach: Reflective outcomes (reasoning, originality, judgement) show in extended/essay answers; classroom must be open and democratic.

concept: Showcase portfolio holds the student's best work
must_teach: Portfolio types: working (work in progress), showcase/display (best pieces selected by student), assessment (work showing achievement of objectives).

concept: Sequence of teaching operations across phases
must_teach: Pre-active: fixing objectives then deciding strategies; interactive: reinforcement during lesson; post-active: changing strategy in light of test results.

concept: Problem-based learning originated in medical education at McMaster University
must_teach: PBL developed at McMaster University medical school, Canada, late 1960s (Howard Barrows); case method linked with Harvard; micro-teaching with Stanford.

concept: CCE scholastic areas relate to academic subjects
must_teach: CCE scholastic areas: curricular subjects and intellectual abilities; co-scholastic: life skills, attitudes, values, health, physical education, cultural activities.

concept: SPOC = Small Private Online Course
must_teach: SPOC uses MOOC-style materials for a limited selected group (e.g. one institution), allows closer interaction, often used for blended teaching.

concept: Disclosing counselling information violates confidentiality
must_teach: Teachers must keep students' personal information private unless disclosure protects the student or others; betrayal damages trust in guidance and counselling.

concept: Prognostic test predicts future performance
must_teach: Prognostic test forecasts likely future performance in a subject/course (guidance, selection); diagnostic finds causes of present errors; summative certifies achievement.

concept: Crowded unreadable chart violates suitability and legibility
must_teach: Support material should be large, clear, simple, accurate and suited to learners' level; novelty, cost and durability are secondary.

concept: Bloom's cognitive levels are hierarchical and cumulative; Handbook I was cognitive
must_teach: Bloom's cognitive levels form a cumulative hierarchy; Handbook I (1956) cognitive; Handbook II (1964, Krathwohl, Bloom, Masia) affective.

concept: Explaining why ice floats using density is an understanding-level question
must_teach: Understanding level: explaining a fact by a principle (seeing relationships); stating values or naming = memory; designing an original test = reflective.

concept: Good teaching needs continuous feedback to adjust instruction
must_teach: Teaching is two-way; feedback from questions, expressions, tests lets teacher match pace, examples and method to learners' understanding.

concept: Learner diagnosing needs, choosing resources and self-assessing = self-directed learning
must_teach: Knowles's self-directed learning: individuals take initiative in diagnosing needs, setting goals, finding resources, choosing strategies, evaluating outcomes; incidental learning is unplanned; programmed learning follows fixed path.

concept: Live video class synchronous; discussion board asynchronous
must_teach: Synchronous: live video class, webinar, instant chat; asynchronous: discussion boards, e-mail, recorded lectures.

concept: Evidence a test measures a theoretical trait is construct validity
must_teach: Construct validity: degree scores reflect a theoretical construct (creativity, intelligence, anxiety), shown by correlations and factor analysis; content validity = sampling of content; predictive = forecasting; face = appearance.
